key_insight: DataMaster introduces a task-conditioned autonomous agent that automates the end-to-end data engineering loop — discovering, adapting, and validating external data — using downstream model feedback to iteratively improve datasets and task performance.
problem_solved: Manual, ad hoc data engineering (searching for datasets, adapting formats/labels, and validating via costly downstream training) is slow, brittle, and hard to scale; DataMaster automates and optimizes that pipeline.
method: Task-conditioned autonomous agent that proposes and executes data-engineering actions (discover, transform, augment, filter) tailored to a target task.
Closed-loop validation: candidate data is validated through proxy or downstream training signals and performance-driven rewards guide selection.
Experience reuse/meta-learning to carry forward strategies and priors from prior tasks, reducing repeated trial-and-error.
impact: Automating data engineering lowers human effort and cost while unlocking consistent, scalable dataset improvements that translate directly into better model performance. Practitioners can iterate faster and focus on higher-level modeling decisions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agent → dataset discovery → transform/clean → downstream training → reward feedback loop to agent
Before/after bar chart showing model performance gains from automated data engineering
Icon set for actions (search, clean, augment, validate) with arrows indicating an iterative loop
Heatmap or timeline showing agent learning/reusing past strategies across tasks
paper_title: DataMaster: Towards Autonomous Data Engineering for Machine Learning
paper_authors: Yaxin Du, Xiyuan Yang, Zhifan Zhou, Wanxu Liu, Zixing Lei
